text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - The Czech ambassador to Slovakia, Rudolf Slansky, said the the former federation partners should sign a declaration on their mutual relations. The two countries plan signing a treaty to settle their financial claims connected to the 1993 split.

- Some 67 percent of Slovak citizens would take part in a referendum on Slovakia's integration into the European Union (EU), of which 82 percent would vote in favour of the country's membership, a public opinion poll showed. About 18 percent of those polled said they would vote against the move.
- The slovak agricultural sector posted an 8.5 billion crown foreign trade deficit last year, two billion crowns greater than in 1995.
- The French-Slovak joint-venture GSM operator Globtel said it had 5,000 customers after five weeks of commercial operation.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The European Union has offered Slovakia 15 billion crowns in financial assistance over the next three years. The funds should go mainly to small and medium-sized entreprises.
- The Slovak government has not yet decided whether it will allow a foreign investor to take a stake in troubled white goods producer Calex.
- Slovakia believes that it would win an international law suit against Hungary over the controversial Gabcikovo dam on the Danube river .
- The Druzhba oil pipeline has transported some 475 million tonnes of Russian crude oil over the 35 years of its operation.

PRAVDA - Jan Slota, leader of a minor government coalition partner, the ultra-right Slovak National Party (SNS) has repeatedly said that early elections are the only way to solve the current disputes inside the ruling coalition.
- Slota said Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar would support early elections if there were enough deputies in parliament (a three-fifths majority would be required) to initiate the move.
